artists.biography:
Tori Amos (born Myra Ellen Amos; August 22, 1963) is an American pianist, singer-songwriter and composer. She is a classically trained musician and possesses a mezzo-soprano vocal range. Amos originally served as the lead singer of 1980s synthpop group Y Kant Tori Read, and as a solo artist was at the forefront of a number of female singer-songwriters in the early 1990s. She was also noteworthy early in her solo career as one of the few alternative rock performers to use a piano as her primary instrument. Some of her charting singles include "Crucify", "Silent All These Years", "God", "Cornflake Girl", "Caught a Lite Sneeze", "Professional Widow", "Spark", "1000 Oceans", and "A Sorta Fairytale", her most commercially successful single in the U.S. to date.
 
As of 2005, Amos had sold 12 million albums worldwide. She has been nominated for several awards, including 8 Grammy Award nominations. Amos was also named one of People Magazine's 50 Most Beautiful People in 1996.

perplexity.description:
Native Invader is the fifteenth studio album by American singer-songwriter Tori Amos, released on September 8, 2017, through Decca Records (Universal Music). Musically, the album blends elements of rock and pop with Amos’s signature piano-driven arrangements, atmospheric textures, and introspective lyrics. The record explores themes of personal and political upheaval, drawing inspiration from both contemporary events and Native American mythology, though Amos has described herself as an observer rather than a voice for First Nations people. The lead single, "Cloud Riders," exemplifies the album’s fusion of poetic storytelling and melodic intensity.

Within Amos’s extensive discography, Native Invader stands as her twelfth album of entirely original material, continuing her tradition of lyrical depth and musical experimentation. The album received generally positive reviews, earning a Metacritic score of 76/100 and a 7.5/10 from Pitchfork, with critics praising its emotional resonance and sonic craftsmanship. To support the release, Amos embarked on the Native Invader Tour, performing across Europe and North America. The album solidified her reputation as a distinctive voice in alternative rock and pop, maintaining her artistic relevance more than two decades into her career.
